label: 011 is the packets largest phase and has no children: 27 files to change, nine new runtime modules, five transports and seven new test files, 311 spec lines against 003s 279, yet 003 is a phase parent with six children and 011 is a leaf. Split it into six children: shared adapter and contract, identity link and roster, approval index and queue, Telegram and Slack, Signal and WhatsApp, conformance and hardening.

declaredCapabilities has no vocabulary: REQ-001 fixes the six contract members and the unsupported result shape but never lists the capability names a transport declares, so the unsupported rule has nothing to test against.

The link record has no field list and no file name in Files to Change: REQ-003 says it records the actor and the provider-asserted sender id, links.json appears only in Data Flow and REQ-019/023, and the Files table names only channel-link.ts.

The durable queue entry has no field list: REQ-013 fixes write-before-IO, unknown-never-retried and the 0/5/25/120/600 s backoff, but the entry fields are unstated while bots channel list prints queue depth from queue/.
REQ-017 promises five conformance rules and enumerates two, so a builder invents three of five; the test file is described only as the five conformance rules on a fake transport.

The approval index files key structure is unstated while its fields are listed: REQ-006 gives action id, item id, channel, conversation, choices and expiresAt but not whether the file is a map keyed by action id or an array.

The per-transport operator prerequisites are a dependency table, not a runbook: no artifact gives the exact scopes, events and webhook fields an operator must set for Telegram, Slack, Signal or WhatsApp.
